title: Parcel Shelf Speaker Removal and Installation
introduction: For a coupe with SYNC 2/SYNC 3, reaching the parcel shelf speaker involves more trim work than speaker work. I treat the trim like overlapping roof tiles: uncover the edges in the right order, and each panel can come away without a wrestling match. This guide explains that access sequence, speaker removal and reassembly. It does not diagnose an audio fault or establish that the speaker needs replacement.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Allow for trim removal on both sides
items.detail: Access requires removing the loadspace trim panels, D-pillar trim panels and parcel shelf. The supporting loadspace illustrations show LHD and the RH side; RHD and the LH side are similar.

items.name: Protect the rear cushion locking tabs
items.detail: Press the locking tabs at the front of the rear seat cushion inward before lifting the cushion. Lifting without pressing them inward may damage the tabs.

items.name: Prepare for controlled tightening
items.detail: Have a torque wrench capable of applying the speaker-bolt tightening specification shown in the connector step.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they may also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The tightening specification appears alongside removal work, so it needs to remain available when the speaker goes back.

edits.text:
Remove the parcel shelf to expose the speaker.
Refer to: Parcel Shelf - Coupe (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why:
The shelf is the last layer of the access work. Begin with [Loadspace Trim Panel - Coupe](#/document/G1692601): on both sides, position the door weatherstrip aside, release the scuff plate clips and remove the scuff plate trim panel. Next remove the rear seat cushion using [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168): move both front seats fully forward, press inward on the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion to release it from the floor, then lift, release and remove the cushion. Pressing the tabs inward is essential; lifting against locked tabs may damage them.

Continue by releasing the rear backrest latches and folding the backrests down. Position the safety belt guides aside, release the loadspace panel clips and remove the panels on both sides. Then use [Parcel Shelf - Coupe](#/document/G1692602): release the D-pillar panel clips, disconnect each tether clip and remove the D-pillar trim panels on both sides. Its illustration shows the RH side; the LH side is similar. Finally remove the parcel shelf pin-type retainers and the shelf. I use the trim drawings to locate the hidden attachments before pulling; a released panel should not still be hanging from its tether.

edits.text: Remove the retaining bolts and free the parcel shelf speaker from its mounting. Disconnect the electrical connector in the following step before taking the speaker away.
edits.why: The illustration highlights the speaker in blue and its fasteners and connector in magenta. These distinguish the mechanical attachments from the electrical connection that still links the speaker to the vehicle.

edits.text:
Disconnect the speaker electrical connector.
During installation, tighten the speaker retaining bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: Disconnecting the plug releases the remaining electrical attachment. The tightening specification controls how firmly the speaker is secured when refitted.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence. Reconnect the electrical connector, position the speaker and install its bolts using the tightening specification above. Refit the parcel shelf and its pin-type retainers, then reconnect the D-pillar tether clips and secure the D-pillar trim panels. Refit the loadspace trim panels and safety belt guides, raise and latch the rear backrests, reinstall the rear seat cushion, then refit the scuff plates and door weatherstrips. Complete the trim work on both sides. During reassembly, make sure the safety belt webbing is not twisted and that the belts and buckles remain accessible to the occupants.
edits.why: Reversing the access sequence restores the overlapping trim in order. I finish by checking belt routing and buckle access: the cabin can look neatly assembled while a buckle is still buried under the cushion.
